quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 5 straight sides and 5 corners?
quests.hint: Picture a square with a little triangle roof added on top.
quests.explanation: A pentagon has exactly 5 straight sides and 5 corners.
quests.funFact: Home plate on a baseball field is actually shaped like a pentagon!

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 6 straight sides and 6 corners?
quests.hint: Think of the little cells bees build inside a honeycomb.
quests.explanation: A hexagon has exactly 6 straight sides and 6 corners.
quests.funFact: Bees build honeycomb cells shaped like hexagons because they fit together perfectly with no gaps.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly 8 straight sides and 8 corners?
quests.hint: Think of the shape drivers see on a red road sign that means stop.
quests.explanation: An octagon has exactly 8 straight sides and 8 corners.
quests.funFact: Stop signs are shaped like octagons so drivers can recognize them even from behind.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches the outline of home plate on a baseball field?
quests.hint: Think of a shape with 5 sides, like a square topped with a point.
quests.explanation: Home plate has 5 straight sides, just like a pentagon!
quests.funFact: Home plate's pentagon shape helps umpires judge exactly where the ball crosses.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches the end of a wooden pencil that keeps it from rolling away?
quests.hint: Think of a shape with 6 flat sides around the edge.
quests.explanation: Many pencils have 6 flat sides, just like a hexagon, so they don't roll off the table!
quests.funFact: A hexagon's flat sides are exactly why hexagonal pencils stay put on a desk.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches a big red stop sign at a busy street corner?
quests.hint: Think of a shape with 8 sides, more than a hexagon.
quests.explanation: A stop sign has 8 straight sides, just like an octagon!
quests.funFact: Stop signs have used the octagon shape in the United States for over 100 years.

quests.instruction: Which of these three shapes has no straight sides at all?
quests.hint: Look for the one shape that curves all the way around with nothing straight.
quests.explanation: A circle is the only shape here with no straight sides anywhere.
quests.funFact: Every other shape in this game, besides circle and oval, is made from straight lines.

quests.instruction: Which shape has one more side than a square?
quests.hint: Start with a square's 4 sides, then add just one more.
quests.explanation: A pentagon has 5 sides, exactly one more than a square's 4 sides.
quests.funFact: Adding sides one at a time turns a square into a pentagon, then a hexagon, and so on.

quests.instruction: Which shape has one more side than a pentagon?
quests.hint: Start with a pentagon's 5 sides, then add just one more.
quests.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides, exactly one more than a pentagon's 5 sides.
quests.funFact: Snowflakes often grow in patterns with six sides, just like a hexagon.

quests.instruction: Which shape has two more sides than a hexagon?
quests.hint: Start with a hexagon's 6 sides, then add two more.
quests.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides, two more than a hexagon's 6 sides.
quests.funFact: Some umbrellas are shaped like octagons when you look straight down at them.

quests.instruction: Which shape has one fewer side than a pentagon?
quests.hint: Start with a pentagon's 5 sides, then take one away.
quests.explanation: A square has 4 sides, exactly one fewer than a pentagon's 5 sides.
quests.funFact: Taking a side away from a pentagon and adjusting the corners gives you a square.

quests.instruction: Which shape has the fewest sides of all the straight-sided shapes you've learned?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with only 3 sides in total.
quests.explanation: A triangle has just 3 sides, fewer than square, pentagon, hexagon, or octagon.
quests.funFact: No matter how many sides you add, you can never make a closed shape with fewer than 3.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches a nut that a bolt screws into?
quests.hint: Think of a shape with 6 flat edges for a wrench to grip.
quests.explanation: Many nuts are shaped with 6 flat sides, just like a hexagon, so wrenches can grip them!
quests.funFact: A hexagon shape lets a wrench turn a nut from six different angles.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches a garden gazebo with many flat walls around a circle base?
quests.hint: Think of a shape with 8 flat sides arranged in a ring.
quests.explanation: Some gazebos are built with 8 flat walls, just like an octagon!
quests.funFact: Octagon-shaped buildings let light and air in from eight different directions.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches a simple house drawing, with a square body and triangle roof combined into one outline?
quests.hint: Think of a square with a pointed triangle roof added on top, making one shape.
quests.explanation: A square body topped with a triangle roof combines into a single 5-sided pentagon outline!
quests.funFact: This is a fun way to see how two shapes can combine to make a brand new one.

quests.instruction: Which of these three shapes curves all the way around with no straight edges?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that is round but stretched, not the polygon options.
quests.explanation: An oval curves smoothly all the way around, unlike the straight-sided shapes here.
quests.funFact: Ovals and circles are the only shapes in this game with zero straight sides.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly twice as many sides as a triangle?
quests.hint: A triangle has 3 sides — this shape has double that number.
quests.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides, exactly double a triangle's 3 sides.
quests.funFact: Honeycomb hexagons fit together so perfectly that bees waste almost no space or wax.

quests.instruction: Which shape has exactly twice as many sides as a square?
quests.hint: A square has 4 sides — this shape has double that number.
quests.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides, exactly double a square's 4 sides.
quests.funFact: Doubling a square's sides and adjusting the corners is one way to picture an octagon.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 5 corners, one more than a shape with only 4?
quests.hint: Count carefully — this shape has just one extra corner compared to a square.
quests.explanation: A pentagon has 5 corners, one more than a square's 4 corners.
quests.funFact: Each time you add a side to a shape, you also add exactly one more corner.

quests.instruction: Which of these three shapes has exactly 4 equal sides, tilted to stand on a point?
quests.hint: Look for the shape shaped like a square that has been turned on its corner.
quests.explanation: A diamond has 4 equal sides, tilted so it stands on one point instead of a flat edge.
quests.funFact: Turning a square 45 degrees is exactly how a diamond shape appears.

quests.instruction: Which shape has an edge you could never measure with a straight ruler along one side?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with absolutely no flat, straight parts.
quests.explanation: A circle's edge is entirely curved, so you could never lay a ruler flat along any part of it.
quests.funFact: Measuring around a circle uses a special curved measurement called circumference.

quests.instruction: Which shape would a stop sign lose if it were redesigned with only 6 sides instead?
quests.hint: Think about the real shape stop signs actually use today.
quests.explanation: Stop signs use 8 sides, so redesigning one with only 6 would turn it into a hexagon instead of an octagon.
quests.funFact: The octagon shape has been used for stop signs so long that drivers recognize it instantly, even at a glance.

quests.instruction: Which of these three shapes has exactly 4 sides, with two pairs that are unequal in length?
quests.hint: Look for the shape that isn't perfectly balanced like a square.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has two pairs of sides, but the pairs are different lengths from each other.
quests.funFact: Doors, books, and windows are almost always shaped like rectangles.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches the pattern seen on a soccer ball's flat panels?
quests.hint: Think of a shape with 6 sides, seen alongside pentagon panels on a ball.
quests.explanation: Soccer balls are covered in hexagon and pentagon panels stitched together.
quests.funFact: A classic soccer ball is made of 20 hexagon panels and 12 pentagon panels.

quests.instruction: Which shape matches a simple drawing of a school crossing sign, wider at the bottom?
quests.hint: Think of a shape with 5 sides, often used to mean caution near schools.
quests.explanation: Some school crossing signs are shaped like a pentagon, with 5 straight sides.
quests.funFact: A pentagon's unusual 5-sided shape helps this sign stand out from square or diamond signs.

quests.instruction: Which of these three shapes has points reaching outward instead of a plain closed outline?
quests.hint: Look for the shape with sharp spikes, not a smooth polygon.
quests.explanation: A star has points reaching outward, unlike the smooth outline of a pentagon or hexagon.
quests.funFact: A classic star shape has 5 points, the same number as the sides on a pentagon.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 8 corners, twice as many as a square?
quests.hint: A square has 4 corners — this shape has double that number.
quests.explanation: An octagon has 8 corners, exactly double a square's 4 corners.
quests.funFact: Every corner on a shape also marks where two straight sides meet.

quests.instruction: Which shape has 6 sides that could tile perfectly across a floor with no gaps?
quests.hint: Think of the same shape bees use to build honeycomb without wasting space.
quests.explanation: Hexagons fit together perfectly with no gaps, just like honeycomb cells.
quests.funFact: Only triangles, squares, and hexagons can tile a floor perfectly on their own.

quests.instruction: Which shape, along with squares and hexagons, can also tile a floor with no gaps at all?
quests.hint: Think of the shape with just 3 sides that also fits together perfectly.
quests.explanation: Triangles, squares, and hexagons are the only regular shapes that tile a floor with no gaps.
quests.funFact: Pentagons, on their own, actually leave awkward gaps when you try to tile them.

quests.instruction: Which shape would leave gaps if you tried to cover a whole floor with only that shape?
quests.hint: Think of the round shape that always leaves curved gaps between copies of itself.
quests.explanation: Circles always leave curved gaps between each other, so they can't tile a floor perfectly alone.
quests.funFact: That's why floor tiles are almost always squares, rectangles, hexagons, or triangles instead of circles.
